name: Chisel
text:
Freeze the current terminology in a single, unchangeable snapshot now—store it as a dated PDF in the shared drive and forbid any edits for six months. Creative, Operations, and Legal all lose the ability to tweak definitions mid-stream, so no group can weaponize the glossary to favor its own goals. The trade-off is that we accept slower adaptation to new terms, but we gain an authoritative baseline everyone must use, eliminating contradictions today.
[dispatched 3 workers: worker-4887, worker-4490, worker-1337 — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: Freezing the glossary now embeds the current power struggle into stone—Legal, Creative, and Operations will each lock their favored definitions, turning the glossary into a battleground, not a tool. Instead, run a one-week sprint where Legal drafts the first version, Creative and Operations each propose one contradiction, then all three negotiate a single revision cycle before locking it. The artifact is the revised glossary and the signed agreement on the revision rules.

name: Scope
text: Run a two-week glossary sprint with an external facilitator. Creative drafts the first version, Operations and Legal each propose three non-negotiable terms they need clarified, then all three negotiate to a single definition. Trade-off: we accept a short delay now to avoid a six-month freeze that entrenches today’s power struggles.

name: Scriv
text: The glossary freeze locks today’s power struggle into policy—Legal, Creative, and Operations will each hardcode their favored terms, turning the document into a battleground, not a tool. Instead, run a two-week sprint with an external facilitator: Creative drafts the first version, Operations and Legal each propose three non-negotiable terms, then all three negotiate to a single definition. The artifact is the signed-off glossary; the decision is final.
